prompt:
I'm going to travel from May 25 to June 29.
First, I'm going to Halle (Saale), Germany.

During my travel I want to visit Italy (Florence, Rom, Pisa, Capri, Milan), Switzerland (Lugano), Netherlands (Amesterdam, Maastricht), Spain (Madrid, Barcelona), France (Paris, Lyon), Germany (Berlin, Dresden) and Prague.

From May 25-May 29 I want to stay in Halle (Saale), Dresden, Leipzig and Berlin.

I want to visit Prague for only two days, only from June 14-June 16.

After visiting Milan, I want to go Lugano straight and come back to Milan.

I also don't want to visit Venice.

I want to have three days in Paris.

I want to go to the Netherlands from either Paris or Berlin.

On June 27 I want to go back to Halle.

Help me to plan my travel.
answer:
| Dates | Overnight base | Travel and sightseeing plan |
|---|---|---|
| **May 25** | **Halle (Saale)** | Arrive and settle in. Explore the old town if time allows. |
| **May 26** | **Leipzig** | Train from Halle, approximately 25–40 minutes. Spend the day exploring central Leipzig. |
| **May 27** | **Dresden** | Train from Leipzig, approximately 1–1½ hours. Visit the Frauenkirche, historic centre and Elbe riverfront. |
| **May 28–29** | **Berlin** | Travel from Dresden on May 28, approximately 2 hours. Use the rest of May 28 and all of May 29 for Berlin. |
| **May 30–31** | **Amsterdam** | Travel **directly from Berlin to the Netherlands**, approximately 6 hours by train. Explore Amsterdam’s canals and museums. |
| **June 1** | **Maastricht** | Train from Amsterdam, approximately 2½ hours. Explore the old town, Vrijthof and riverside. |
| **June 2–5** | **Paris** | Travel from Maastricht on June 2, usually via Liège or Brussels. **June 3, 4 and 5 are three full sightseeing days in Paris.** |
| **June 6** | **Lyon** | Morning train from Paris, approximately 2 hours. Spend the afternoon and evening in Vieux Lyon and around Fourvière. |
| **June 7–10** | **Barcelona** | Travel from Lyon on June 7; a direct train takes approximately 5 hours when available. June 8–10 gives you three full days for Gaudí’s buildings, the Gothic Quarter and the waterfront. |
| **June 11–13** | **Madrid** | High-speed train from Barcelona on June 11, approximately 2½–3 hours. Visit the Prado, Retiro Park and Royal Palace over the following days. |
| **June 14–15** | **Prague** | Fly from Madrid on June 14. Explore Prague on June 14–15, stay two nights, and **leave on the morning of June 16**. |
| **June 16–17** | **Naples** | Travel from Prague to Naples on June 16. On **June 17, visit Capri by ferry**, returning to Naples that evening. Naples is a convenient base that avoids moving your luggage onto the island. |
| **June 18–20** | **Rome** | Train from Naples on June 18, approximately 1¼ hours. Spend June 19–20 visiting ancient Rome, the Vatican and the historic centre. |
| **June 21–23** | **Florence** | Train from Rome on June 21, approximately 1½ hours. Explore Florence on June 21–22; take a **Pisa day trip on June 23**, approximately 1 hour each way. |
| **June 24–26** | **Milan** | Travel from Florence on June 24, approximately 2 hours, and explore Milan. On **June 25, take a direct train to Lugano and return directly to Milan**, approximately 1¼–1½ hours each way. June 26 is another day in Milan. |
| **June 27–28** | **Halle (Saale)** | **Return to Halle on June 27.** A practical option is flying from Milan to Frankfurt, then taking a train to Halle. Allow most of the day for the journey. Rest in Halle on June 28. |
| **June 29** | — | Departure or onward travel from Halle. |

Prague’s **June 14–16 window is treated as two nights**, with sightseeing on June 14–15 and departure on June 16. Venice is omitted.

The route follows a sensible geographical order: Germany → Netherlands → France → Spain → Prague → southern Italy → northern Italy → Halle. Capri comes before Rome so that your Italian journey then continues north toward Florence and Milan.

Before booking accommodation, check these transport connections:

- **Madrid → Prague, June 14:** choose an early flight to preserve sightseeing time.
- **Prague → Naples, June 16:** check whether a direct flight operates that day. An alternative is flying to Rome and continuing to Naples by train.
- **Lyon → Barcelona, June 7:** direct trains can be limited; a connection may be necessary.
- **Milan → Germany, June 27:** choose a flight with enough time for the onward train to Halle.

All journey times are approximate. For sightseeing, reserve popular timed-entry attractions ahead, especially the Eiffel Tower/Louvre, Sagrada Família, Vatican Museums, Uffizi and Milan’s *Last Supper*.
